summary: This PROJEXA-side diff adds Permits/Drawings/Documents/MoMs UI and thin proxy routes, and does not touch .github/workflows/**, but the worker's own PROGRESS.md discloses that the compliance-tracker backend endpoints these new routes depend on (/api/v1/projexa/drawings, /api/v1/projexa/permits POST, /api/v1/projexa/veri-meetings*, /api/v1/documents POST) were built in an isolated worktree that was never committed, pushed, or opened as a PR -- meaning an autonomous merge of this PROJEXA diff right now would ship UI and proxy code that calls upstream endpoints that do not yet exist in production, breaking all four new/changed pages (Drawings, MoMs, Permits create, Documents upload) until a separate compliance-tracker PR is authored, reviewed, and merged. Compounding this, PROGRESS.md also admits `npx tsc --noEmit` and `bun test` were never run against the PROJEXA changes in this diff, and no route-level tests were added for the new/edited proxy routes despite an existing repo convention for exactly that (cited in PROGRESS.md itself). The architectural reasoning for reusing the compliance-tracker `documents` table instead of forking new tables is sound on its face, but cannot be verified here since no compliance-tracker diff is included in this review. Given the unverified cross-repo dependency, the admitted lack of build/test verification, and missing tests for new endpoints, this should not be merged autonomously as tier1; it needs the compliance-tracker PR landed and verified first, plus a real PROJEXA-side tsc/test pass, before reconsideration.
issues: New/changed PROJEXA proxy routes (api/drawings, api/permits POST, api/documents POST, api/moms/*) call compliance-tracker endpoints that PROGRESS.md says were never committed, pushed, or opened as a PR in compliance-tracker -- merging this now risks shipping UI that 404s/breaks in production until that separate backend PR lands.

PROGRESS.md explicitly states `npx tsc --noEmit` and `bun test` were NOT run against the PROJEXA-side changes in this diff -- no build/test verification exists for the code being proposed for autonomous merge.

No route-level tests were added for the new/edited proxy routes (permits POST, drawings GET/POST, documents POST, moms/route.ts, moms/[id]/*), despite the repo's own established convention for testing exactly this kind of thin proxy route (cited by the worker's own PROGRESS.md).

The diff text supplied for this review is truncated/incomplete (PermitsClient.tsx and veridian-client.ts, including the new callVeridianUpload multipart-upload helper, are not fully shown), so upload-path handling (content-type, size limits, header forwarding) could not be fully verified.
No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff -- the hard workflow-file rule does not apply here.
